subject: Using fscores with WLE on a testlet model

messages.author: 6096f5087826f400
messages.subject: Using fscores with WLE on a testlet model
parts:
Hello All,

I am conducting research on the application of higher order IRT models (which can be shown to be algebraically related to the testlet model) and I want to obtain theta estimates using the weighted likelihood estimation method. However, when using the WLE method fscores returns NA for all theta estimates (both the general and the testlet). I read through Warm's paper and I was unable to find any section that provided guidance on this issue.

Does anyone have any suggestions on how to proceed? For reproducibility I included Phil's code below for the testlet model along with the fscores call.

Thank you.

---
library(mirt)

# General testlet response model (Wainer, 2007)
#simulate data
set.seed(1234)
a <- matrix(0, 12, 4)
a[,1] <- rlnorm(12, .2, .3)
ind <- 1
for(i in 1:3){
  a[ind:(ind+3),i+1] <- a[ind:(ind+3),1]
  ind <- ind+4
}
print(a)
d <- rnorm(12, 0, .5)
sigma <- diag(c(1, .5, 1, .5))
dataset <- simdata(a,d,2000,itemtype=rep('2PL', 12),sigma=sigma)
itemstats(dataset)
# estimate by applying constraints and freeing the latent variances
specific <- c(rep(1,4),rep(2,4), rep(3,4))
model <- "G = 1-12
CONSTRAIN = (1, a1, a2), (2, a1, a2), (3, a1, a2), (4, a1, a2),
(5, a1, a3), (6, a1, a3), (7, a1, a3), (8, a1, a3),
(9, a1, a4), (10, a1, a4), (11, a1, a4), (12, a1, a4)
COV = S1*S1, S2*S2, S3*S3"
simmod <- bfactor(dataset, specific, model)

fscores(simmod, method = "WLE")

-----

Warning message: NAs returned for response patterns with no data. Consider removing

G S1 S2 S3 [1,] NA NA NA NA [2,] NA NA NA NA [3,] NA NA NA NA [4,] NA NA NA NA

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Using fscores with WLE on a testlet model
parts:
Hi Yale,

I believe this is expected behaviour with no work around. The WLE estimator requires computing the determinant of the observed information matrix which, for the testlet model and friends, is non-positive definite given the implied constraints. You should have seen many warnings pop up in your R console to indicate this information. Hence, for these particularly constrained models you'll have to stick with some of the more basic estimators for now (I'd recommend MAPs). HTH.

Phil
